Model Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27

A complete, adaptable TMSS covering every requirement of the CIPFA Treasury Management and Prudential Codes (2021) — written as the document a council would take to full council, with a consistent worked example throughout.

All figures are illustrative ("Exampleshire Council", a unitary authority with retained housing stock) — replace throughout with your authority's own. Passages marked after a named council adapt that council's published 2025/26–2026/27 strategy, identified from the 37 strategies scored on this site; the strongest overall were Westminster City Council, Redcar and Cleveland, Cheshire East Council.
Authority type: Sections badged "HRA authorities" apply only where housing stock is retained; stock-transfer districts and counties can hide them.

1 · Introduction, adoption and governance

after Herefordshire · North Northamptonshire Council · Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole (BCP Council)

This Council has adopted the four clauses of CIPFA's Treasury Management in the Public Services: Code of Practice (2021 Edition), and maintains as its framework: a Treasury Management Policy Statement defining the policies and objectives of its treasury activities; suitable Treasury Management Practices (TMPs) with supporting schedules; the reporting cycle in section 12; and delegation of the execution and administration of treasury decisions to the Section 151 Officer, who acts in accordance with the Policy Statement, TMPs and CIPFA's Standard of Professional Practice.

Policy statement. The Council defines its treasury management activities as the management of the organisation's borrowing, investments and cash flows, its banking, money market and capital market transactions, the effective control of the risks associated with those activities, and the pursuit of optimum performance consistent with those risks. The Council regards the successful identification, monitoring and control of risk as the prime criterion by which the effectiveness of treasury activities is measured; value for money is a secondary objective pursued within that risk framework.

Approval and scrutiny. This strategy is approved by full council before the start of the financial year, on the recommendation of Cabinet. The Audit & Governance Committee is nominated as the body responsible for effective scrutiny of the treasury function and receives every report in the cycle before or alongside the decision-making body. The prudential indicators in section 9 are set, and may only be amended, by full council.

Third-party funds. Monies held on behalf of the Exampleshire Pension Fund and jointly managed trust funds are identified separately and managed under the same standards of care, with their own counterparty records.

2 · External context and interest-rate outlook

[Insert, at the point of drafting: the Bank Rate level and market-implied path, gilt-yield levels and your treasury advisor's central forecast, and the PWLB certainty-rate margins. State the date of the forecast. The live market position for this is maintained on the Pulse tab of this site.]

The strategy below is written to be robust to the forecast being wrong in either direction: borrowing decisions are framed against the liability benchmark (section 5), and the interest-rate exposure limits in section 11 cap the revenue impact of adverse moves.

The capital financing requirement (CFR) is the Council's underlying need to borrow for capital purposes. HRA rows apply to stock-holding authorities only.

Gross debt and the CFR. Gross external debt (£455m) does not exceed the total CFR (£598m), and is not expected to exceed the CFR over the three-year horizon — the key Prudential Code test that borrowing is for capital purposes only. The gap is internal borrowing: £143m of the borrowing need is currently met from the Council's own reserves and working capital, a position kept under review against the liability benchmark and the investment balances it consumes.

4 · Borrowing strategy

after Redcar and Cleveland · North Northamptonshire Council

The Council borrows only in sterling, and only for the purposes permitted by the Prudential Code: capital expenditure, refinancing maturing debt, and short-term cash-flow management. The Council will not borrow in advance of need purely to profit from the investment of the sums borrowed; where borrowing is undertaken ahead of a firm requirement (for example to de-risk a known refinancing peak) the decision and its carry cost are reported in the next mid-year or outturn report.

Debt limits set by full councilBorrowing £mOther long-term liabilities £mTotal £m
Authorised limit 2026/2766045705
Operational boundary 2026/2761540655

The authorised limit is the statutory ceiling (s3, Local Government Act 2003) that external debt must not breach; the operational boundary is the expected working maximum — a breach of the boundary triggers investigation, a breach of the limit is unlawful. Other long-term liabilities cover PFI and finance-lease obligations.

2026/27 borrowing need. £58m of new borrowing is planned (new capital £26m, refinancing £32m of maturing loans). The default instrument is PWLB certainty-rate maturity loans, tested against forward market alternatives at the point of drawing; maturities are chosen to fill the troughs in the maturity profile (section 9) rather than to chase the cheapest point on the curve, so refinancing exposure in any one year stays within the limits in section 11.

Gross vs net. The Council manages borrowing against the gross requirement, alongside a net position kept deliberately: internal borrowing is run down only as investment balances allow while maintaining the liquidity floor in section 7.

The liability benchmark

after Redcar and Cleveland

The Council's core borrowing decisions are framed against the liability benchmark — the projection of existing debt against the future need for borrowing, assuming minimum investment balances of £30m. Where existing debt falls below the benchmark, the gap is the future borrowing requirement; debt above the benchmark would indicate over-borrowing. At 31 March 2026 existing loans run £143m below the benchmark within three years, which is the basis of the refinancing plan above. [Insert the benchmark chart here — plotted for at least ten years, and ideally the full life of the debt portfolio.]

HRA authorities Separate liability benchmarks are maintained and presented for the General Fund and the HRA, so each account's borrowing need is visible on its own.

5 · Housing Revenue Account treasury management HRA authorities

after Redcar and Cleveland · Slough Borough Council

The Council operates a two-pool approach: loans are assigned at inception to either the General Fund or the HRA pool, and interest costs follow the assignment. Borrowing shared across both accounts is split on the CFR ratio at the point of drawing. The Item 8 determination governs the charge of interest between the accounts; the average rate on the HRA pool (4.12% illustrative) is applied to the HRA CFR of £186m.

6 · Treasury investment strategy

after Redcar and Cleveland · Telford and Wrekin

The Council's investment priorities, in order, are security, then liquidity, then yield ("SLY"). Investments are made prudently with public money; yield is pursued only within the security and liquidity constraints below, and the Council does not borrow to invest for yield.

Approved counterpartiesMinimum credit criteriaCash limitMax duration
UK Government (DMADF, T-bills, gilts)n/a — sovereignUnlimited6 months (DMADF) / 5 years (gilts)
UK local authoritiesn/a — statutory£10m each2 years
UK banks — ring-fencedA− / A3 long-term£15m each12 months
Building societiesA− / A3£10m each6 months
Money market funds (CNAV/LVNAV)AAA (mmf)£20m each, £60m totalinstant access
Non-UK sovereign banksAA− sovereign, A− bank£10m per country6 months

Credit criteria use the lowest of the three main agencies' ratings; ratings are monitored daily via the treasury advisor with watch/outlook taken into account, and a downgrade below criteria stops new lending and triggers recall-at-maturity.

Specified and non-specified investments. Specified investments (sterling, <365 days, high credit quality per the table) are the default. Non-specified investments — anything longer than a year, the £25m strategic pooled-fund allocation, and any lower-rated instrument — are capped at £45m in aggregate with the long-term limit in section 9.

Liquidity. A minimum of £30m is held in instant-access or <100-day instruments, sized on the cash-flow forecast's worst fortnight over the last three years.

MiFID II. The Council has opted up to professional client status with its brokers and fund providers, and holds the balance-sheet and experience evidence for that election.

7 · Commercial and non-treasury investments

after Redcar and Cleveland

The Council holds a small legacy portfolio of service and commercial property investments (book value £18m, 1.9% of the balance sheet). In line with the Prudential Code (2021) the Council does not borrow to invest primarily for financial return, treats the portfolio as proportionate to its resources, reviews annually the options to exit each holding against sunk-cost and market conditions, and reports the portfolio's performance, valuation movement and cover ratios separately from treasury investments in the reporting cycle. New commercial investment for yield is not permitted under this strategy.

Authorities with no such holdings: replace this section with a one-line statement that the authority holds no service or commercial investments for yield — the Code still requires the statement.

8 · Minimum revenue provision statement

after Isle of Wight Council · Redcar and Cleveland · West Berkshire Council

MRP is the prudent annual charge to revenue for the repayment of debt-financed capital expenditure. Full council approves this statement annually before the year begins.

Expenditure typeMRP method 2026/27
Pre-2008 borrowing (supported)2% of opening CFR, straight line
Post-2008 unsupported borrowingAsset-life annuity, PWLB rate at inception
Finance leases & PFICharge equal to the principal element of the rental
Capital loans to third partiesAnnuity over the loan term; expected-credit-loss reviewed annually

MRP begins in the year after the asset becomes operational. Overpayments (VRP) may be made and reclaimed only as permitted by the statutory guidance, and any change of method is applied prospectively with the comparison disclosed. HRA authorities No MRP is charged to the HRA; the HRA makes provision through depreciation and the voluntary repayment policy in the HRA business plan. The MRP charge and method are disclosed in the statement of accounts.

10 · Borrowing and investment in context: affordability

The capital programme this strategy finances is affordable within the Council's revenue budget and reserves strategy: the incremental revenue cost of the 2026/27 borrowing plan is £2.9m by 2028/29 (2.1% of net revenue), provided for in the MTFS. Affordability is re-assessed in every quarterly indicator report, and the capital programme — not the treasury strategy — is the corrective lever if financing costs breach the tolerance of 9% of net revenue.

11 · Risk management

after Medway Council · Redcar and Cleveland · North Northamptonshire Council

TMP1 identifies and manages the nine treasury risks: credit and counterparty, liquidity, interest rate, exchange rate, refinancing, legal and regulatory, operational (fraud, error, corruption — including payment controls and segregation of duties), market, and inflation. The full TMP schedules record the control for each; the material exposures are:

Interest-rate risk. The Council's exposure is measured as the revenue impact of an immediate ±1% move in rates on variable-rate debt, investments and the year's refinancing: +1% costs £0.58m/yr on current projections (−1% saves £0.51m). Variable-rate debt is capped at 20% of total debt. The Council does not use standalone derivatives; embedded options (the £20m LOBO) are managed on the prudent call-date basis above, and any future derivative use would require a policy amendment approved by full council.

Refinancing risk. No more than 25% of debt may mature in any rolling 24-month window (section 9); the 2026/27 plan pre-funds the March 2027 £18m maturity peak in the autumn if forward rates are at or below the budget assumption.

Credit risk. Managed through the counterparty framework in section 6, daily rating monitoring, and exposure reporting by counterparty group in every cycle report. Guarantees and contingent commitments given by the Council are re-identified each year and listed in the TMP schedules.

after Redcar and Cleveland · Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole (BCP Council)

ReportAudienceTiming

Where external audit qualifies or delays the accounts, the affected figures are flagged as unaudited in every report until resolved.

after North Northamptonshire Council · City of York Council

Knowledge and skills. Members taking treasury decisions and officers executing them receive training at least annually, with attendance recorded and reported; new Audit & Governance members receive induction training before their first treasury report. Officer CPD follows the CIPFA Code of Practice; where in-house capacity is insufficient the Council buys advice, but responsibility for decisions always remains with the Council, and the treasury advisor's performance is reviewed annually against its contract (TMP11).

after Rutland County Council

ESG. Within the SLY framework the Council prefers, at equal risk and return, counterparties and instruments with stronger environmental and social profiles; ESG ratings inform but do not replace credit criteria. The Council will not knowingly invest directly in [state exclusions — e.g. fossil-fuel extraction] and reviews this policy annually.
